title: One ticket, one run
needs: About 150 MB of disk for the Temporal packages
goal: Make every trigger for the same ticket land in one Temporal run, by naming the run after the ticket and joining the run that is already open.

guess.q: The Jira poll, Slack /nova and a Jira comment all ask Nova to work on the same ticket within one minute. The run's ID is nova:RH-1234 and you did not set a conflict policy. What happens?

options.text: Three runs start, and Nova does the work three times.
options.why: Temporal never keeps two open runs with the same ID, so a fixed ID makes this impossible.

options.text: The first trigger starts the run, and the second and third get a WorkflowExecutionAlreadyStartedError.
options.why: That is Temporal's default: it refuses a second start while the run is open. USE_EXISTING turns that error into "here is the run that is already open".

options.text: The last trigger wins: it stops the first run and starts a new one.
options.why: That is TERMINATE_EXISTING, which you must ask for. It is never the default, and the platform never uses it, because it throws work away.

follow.say: Now see what Temporal does with the same ID twice when you set no policy, because USE_EXISTING will replace this error.
follow.see:
first start  → ID demo:RH-1234   run b7492f2e
second start → WorkflowExecutionAlreadyStartedError

With a fixed ID, Temporal refuses a second open run. Its default answer is this error.
USE_EXISTING changes the answer: "here is the run that is already open".

build: Open start-run.mjs and change three options: workflowId becomes `${agent}:${thing}`, taskQueue becomes `ai-agents-${agent}`, and add workflowIdConflictPolicy: WorkflowIdConflictPolicy.USE_EXISTING. Run node clean.mjs && node triggers.mjs: all three triggers now show the ID nova:RH-1234 with the same run, and the summary says 3 triggers for RH-1234 → 1 run. Approve that run to finish the story, temporal workflow signal --workflow-id nova:RH-1234 --name approve --input '"Dana"', and watch the worker terminal say "Dana approved RH-1234". Finish with ./academy check while the dev server is still running.
fix: Someone wanted the newest trigger to win, so they changed one word in startRun. Today Nova worked on a ticket for 40 minutes, then Sean typed /nova in Slack to ask how it was going, and Nova started again from zero. Run node clean.mjs && node triggers.mjs --fix to see two TERMINATED runs, then repair fix/start-run.mjs so a new trigger joins the open run.
explain: Why is the run's workflow ID nova:RH-1234 and not a random ID?
A second trigger arrives while the run is still open. What does each policy do: the default (FAIL), USE_EXISTING, and TERMINATE_EXISTING?
Why should the platform never use TERMINATE_EXISTING for an agent's run?
done: Three triggers for one ticket show one run, ./academy check passes, and you stopped the worker and the dev server with Ctrl+C.
